title: At Least 8 Killed as Bus Plunges Into 100-Metre Gorge in Tehri Garhwal
excerpt: The Haridwar-Chamoli bus lost control near Gular Bazar at about 4:30 a.m. on Tuesday and fell below the bridge on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway; 26 injured passengers were pulled out as the rescue continued.
body:
• At least eight people were killed and 26 injured when a passenger bus fell into a gorge nearly 100 metres deep near Gular Bazar in Uttarakhand's Tehri Garhwal district early on Tuesday, November 17.
  • The bus, carrying around 30 to 35 passengers from Haridwar towards Chamoli, lost control at about 4:30 a.m. and went off the road below Gular bridge, on the Rishikesh-Badrinath National Highway.
  • State Disaster Response Force teams from Byasi and Dhalwala carried out the rescue; the district magistrate and the senior superintendent of police travelled to the site to oversee relief.
  • The toll rose through the morning as rescuers pulled survivors from the wreckage, and officials said the operation was continuing.

At least eight people were killed and 26 others injured after a passenger bus plunged into a gorge nearly 100 metres deep in Uttarakhand's Tehri Garhwal district early on Tuesday, according to reports from the scene. The bus lost control near Gular Bazar at about 4:30 a.m. and fell below Gular bridge, on the Rishikesh-Badrinath National Highway.

Around 30 to 35 people were travelling in the bus, which was on its way from Haridwar to Chamoli, NDTV reported. Rescuers pulled the injured from the wreckage and shifted them to hospitals in ambulances. The reported toll climbed as the morning progressed: an early police update spoke of 20 injured rescued, and the count of the dead rose from six to at least eight in later reports, with the rescue operation still under way.

Rescue operation

Teams of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) from its posts at Byasi and Dhalwala were deployed to the gorge soon after the accident and launched a search and rescue operation. Tehri District Magistrate Nitika Khandelwal and Senior Superintendent of Police Shweta Choubey left for the accident site to oversee the rescue and relief work, both NDTV and The Times of India reported.

"Deeply disturbed to learn about the loss of lives due to a mishap in Tehri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand. I extend my deepest condolences to the bereaved families in this hour of grief."

- Narendra Modi, Prime Minister, via PMO India on X

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami also expressed grief over the casualties and said he had directed officials to ensure the injured receive proper medical treatment and that all possible assistance is provided to those affected. Neither report carried an announcement of compensation for the victims' families.

A difficult stretch of highway

The crash happened on the Rishikesh-Badrinath National Highway, the mountain road that carries pilgrims and tourists towards Badrinath and the upper reaches of Chamoli district, and a route also used by NRI families visiting the Char Dham shrines. The chief minister's statement referred to casualties in more than one road accident in the region the same morning, underlining the risks on these hill roads in the dark early hours. What caused the bus to leave the road near Gular has not yet been stated by officials.

What happens next

Rescue work at the gorge was continuing as of the latest reports, and officials have not yet released the names of the dead or a final count of those on board. The district administration is expected to confirm the toll once the operation concludes and the injured have been accounted for at the hospitals treating them.
image_caption: The wrecked bus lies in a stream at the bottom of the gorge near Gular Bazar in Tehri Garhwal, with police and rescue personnel at the scene. The Haridwar to Chamoli bus fell nearly 100 metres from the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway early on Tuesday, killing at least eight people.
nri_angle: The crash was on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway, the Char Dham pilgrim route also used by NRI families visiting Uttarakhand.
